dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The station's water recycling system is failing. The archive's drones stripped a critical pump relay three nights ago. The station AI reports the system as nominal, because the relay was outside its monitoring scope. Residents are rationing water.

dialogue.speaker: aguilar
dialogue.text: AGUILAR: You're dispatch? Good. The archive's bots took our water relay. We've been on reserves for three days. Population two hundred and six, supply days four, at current rationing.

dialogue.speaker: protagonist
dialogue.text: Show me the junction.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Aguilar meets you at the relay junction. Brief, transactional. The stripped relay housing is clean, almost surgical.

dialogue.speaker: protagonist
dialogue.text: I can restore this. Full capacity takes components I'd have to leave here. Partial keeps the crisis stopped without emptying my kit.

choices.label: Restore the relay to full capacity

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Two hours of work. The water relay comes back online at full capacity, and the rationing board comes off the wall.

dialogue.speaker: aguilar
dialogue.text: AGUILAR: We'll log this. If your route comes back through, there's a standing resource allocation for relay personnel.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The relay comes back at sixty percent capacity. Enough to stop the crisis. Not enough to forget it.

dialogue.speaker: aguilar
dialogue.text: AGUILAR: Understood. Thank you for what you could do. The allocation stands, at reduced weight.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You log the fault, reference number and timestamp, and explain the situation. Aguilar's expression doesn't change.

dialogue.speaker: aguilar
dialogue.text: AGUILAR: So we wait.

dialogue.speaker: protagonist
dialogue.text: The documentation helps when repair crews come through.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You continue. The intrusion clock ticks forward.

rewards.label: Standing Allocation
rewards.description: Aguilar releases relay-grade components from the station's controlled stock.

rewards.label: Rationing Board Records
rewards.description: Six days of consumption data showing exactly when and where the archive's bots drew power for the strip.

rewards.label: Service Corridor
rewards.description: Aguilar opens a monitored maintenance corridor the archive's sweep ignores, buying {amount} clock units.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Two adjacent communities share a generator hub. The archive took one of the two distribution nodes. Now they're arguing over who gets primary access to what remains.

dialogue.speaker: engineer
dialogue.text: ENGINEER: Medical equipment has priority. I've been saying it for three days.

dialogue.speaker: aguilar
dialogue.text: AGUILAR: And we have three hundred people on pump-dependent water filtration. What's the triage protocol for dehydration?

dialogue.speaker: dex
dialogue.text: DEX: Been watching this for a week. Nobody's wrong. That's the problem.

dialogue.speaker: protagonist
dialogue.text: I can't restore the missing node. But I can reconfigure the distribution system to run both loads on the remaining node at reduced efficiency.

dialogue.speaker: engineer
dialogue.text: ENGINEER: Seventy percent each keeps the medical equipment running.

dialogue.speaker: aguilar
dialogue.text: AGUILAR: Seventy percent keeps the filtration pumps running. Do it.

choices.label: Arbitrate a rotation and move on

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You recognize the distribution architecture on sight. The reconfiguration takes twenty minutes of efficient work. Both communities get their reduced-capacity load, and nobody's medical equipment or water filtration is failing.

dialogue.speaker: dex
dialogue.text: DEX: Clean. You want route intel for the eastern tunnels, I owe you one anyway.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The reconfiguration works, but it takes longer and costs more components than it should have. The distribution holds at sixty-five percent each. Close enough.

dialogue.speaker: dex
dialogue.text: DEX: Ugly, but it'll hold. Route intel's still on offer, if you're going east.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You set the distribution to alternate in six-hour blocks. Neither side is satisfied, but neither side is losing essential services. You log the situation and move.

dialogue.speaker: aguilar
dialogue.text: AGUILAR: Dispatch will hear about this.

dialogue.speaker: protagonist
dialogue.text: I hope so. Tell them what the archive took.

dialogue.speaker: dex
dialogue.text: DEX: For what it's worth, you read the room right. Eastern tunnel intel's yours if you want it.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The route continues.

rewards.label: Engineering Cache
rewards.description: The station engineer's spare components, released with both communities' grudging blessing.

rewards.label: Dex's Route Intel
rewards.description: The scrapper's hand-corrected maps of the eastern maintenance network, marks where the bots work and when.

rewards.label: Dead Power Run
rewards.description: Dex knows a decommissioned feeder the archive's monitoring sweep never covers, buying {amount} clock units.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Residents from a downstream station have arrived, fleeing degrading conditions caused by the archive's salvage cascade. They have firsthand accounts of what's happening further along your route.

dialogue.speaker: sato
dialogue.text: SATO: The station AI allocated additional ventilation to the intake area before they arrived. It anticipated the load increase from atmospheric sensor data. That's what it does. It keeps the air moving.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Sato is organizing the newcomers with calm efficiency. The receiving station needs help managing the influx, and the refugees know things.

dialogue.speaker: sato
dialogue.text: SATO: They describe systematic component removal. Not random scavenging. Bot activity unlike anything the tunnel runners report.

choices.label: Help stabilize the station and debrief the refugees

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You spend a cycle on relay work, stabilizing the receiving station's systems under the increased load. In exchange, the refugees talk freely.

dialogue.speaker: sato
dialogue.text: SATO: You have their gratitude and their information. The section they fled is three stops further along your route. Consider what they left behind.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You interview the refugees. The intelligence is the same, and so is the warning.

dialogue.speaker: sato
dialogue.text: SATO: You have your information. They need someone to fix the lighting in the intake corridor.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You keep your pace and your components. The intake corridor's lights stay dark behind you as you pass.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The route continues.

rewards.label: Refugee Salvage
rewards.description: Components the newcomers carried out of their failing station, traded for the work you did.

rewards.label: Firsthand Accounts
rewards.description: Consistent testimony from the refugees: the bots strip methodically, at night, always toward the facility.

rewards.label: Cleared Passage
rewards.description: Sato's community clears and staffs a shortcut through their section, gaining {amount} clock units.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: A station AI is behaving erratically: opening and closing doors in sequence, cycling ventilation between zones, running maintenance checks on equipment that doesn't exist anymore. The equipment it's checking was removed by the archive's bots, but its asset registry hasn't been updated. It's trying to service ghosts.

dialogue.speaker: dex
dialogue.text: DEX: Been watching this one for days. Trade's simple: you fix it, I get a station that stops cycling air like it's drunk. Residents have gotten used to it. It's getting worse.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Doors cycle. Ventilation hums and stops. The station AI's confusion is manifesting as physical infrastructure behavior.

dialogue.speaker: protagonist
dialogue.text: Its asset registry still lists every component the archive stripped. If I patch the registry to match reality, the behavior should stop. If I just watch, I learn the pattern but the ghosts stay.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You patch the asset registry. The AI stabilizes immediately, and the doors hold. The registry's missing-equipment list tells its own story: a systematic harvest radiating outward from the maintenance tunnels.

dialogue.speaker: protagonist
dialogue.text: This is the first concrete evidence of the archive's method. Every strip, timestamped by the victim's own system.

dialogue.speaker: dex
dialogue.text: DEX: Knew it was a pattern. Didn't want to be right.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You document the behavior pattern without intervention. The information is useful but incomplete. The doors keep cycling behind you.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You move on. The doors keep cycling.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The route continues.

rewards.label: Dex's Trade
rewards.description: Components from the scrapper's personal stash, payment for quiet work.

rewards.label: Registry Discrepancies
rewards.description: The station AI's full maintenance history, cross-referenced against what actually remains.

rewards.label: Blind Vent Zone
rewards.description: Dex shows you a ventilation dead zone the archive's sweep treats as background noise, worth {amount} clock units.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: A junction point where you can reroute power to stabilize a struggling station, or keep power flowing toward the facility approach corridor, making your own route easier. The choice is visible and the consequences are immediate.

dialogue.speaker: dex
dialogue.text: DEX: This feeds the district's backup grid. The archive tapped it two days ago; it's pulling forty percent of the output toward the facility corridor. I can show you the tap.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The junction hums. Cutting the archive's tap restores the district's backup capacity. Leaving it means fewer obstacles on your own approach.

dialogue.speaker: protagonist
dialogue.text: The tap's architecture is documented, if you know how to read it. Read it right, and you can reroute power and cover the traces.

choices.label: Leave the routing as it is
Reroute and sabotage the archive's tap

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You disconnect the archive's tap and bridge the circuit with a module from your kit. Full power flows back to the district's backup grid.

dialogue.speaker: dex
dialogue.text: DEX: The district owes you one. Might not know it, but they do.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You leave the archive's tap in place. More power on your route means fewer obstacles between you and the facility.

dialogue.speaker: dex
dialogue.text: DEX: Your call, Relay. He logs it in his own records, whatever those are for.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Somewhere behind you, a backup grid runs at sixty percent. It will not be enough, later, when it is needed.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You recognize the tap's monitoring architecture and sabotage its reporting while you reroute. Power restored, traces cold.

dialogue.speaker: protagonist
dialogue.text: The archive's sweep won't flag this junction for a full maintenance cycle. That's time. That's clock.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The junction is behind you. The route continues.

rewards.label: Junction Locker
rewards.description: A maintenance locker at the junction, opened with the district's standing permission.

rewards.label: Load Flow Analysis
rewards.description: The archive's power draw, mapped: magnitude, schedule, and destination bearing.

rewards.label: Sabotaged Sweep
rewards.description: The monitoring you corrupted buys {amount} clock units before the archive notices the junction went quiet.

dialogue.speaker: protagonist
dialogue.text: Junction 4-B feeds the district's secondary filtration loop. The conduit crosses the tunnel here, blocking the crawl. If I cut it, I get a clean bypass module and the path clears. The district loses redundancy.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: No one is here. No one will know why their backup failed, when it fails. You will.

choices.label: Cut the conduit and take the module

dialogue.speaker: protagonist
dialogue.text: Clean cut. The module goes in the kit. The district's filtration drops to single-loop. They won't notice until something else fails.

dialogue.speaker: protagonist
dialogue.text: Spent a module to bridge around the obstruction. The district keeps their backup. My kit's lighter.

dialogue.speaker: protagonist
dialogue.text: Twenty minutes of crawling through conduit brackets. The path's clear. The conduit's intact. My clock isn't.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The tunnel continues.

rewards.label: Sidewall Cache
rewards.description: A technician's hide-from-the-clock cache, sealed into the tunnel wall years ago.

rewards.label: Conduit Manifest
rewards.description: Stamped ratings on the stripped feeds, a record of what the archive considers worth taking.

rewards.label: Quiet Section
rewards.description: A stretch of tunnel the archive's sweep crosses slowly, buying {amount} clock units.

dialogue.speaker: protagonist
dialogue.text: The bots cleared a path here. Not for humans, for themselves. The clearance is tight but passable. The depot on the left looks untouched.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: A collapsed section has been partially cleared by the archive's bots, creating a path that's usable but unstable. An intact depot nearby may still hold something.

choices.label: Stabilize the passage and push through

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The archive's bots have been here, but only took what matched their parts manifest. Everything else is still on the shelves: components, and maintenance records worth more than the components.

dialogue.speaker: protagonist
dialogue.text: Used a module to shore up the passage. Clean transit, no surprises.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The longer route costs time, but the infrastructure patterns along it reveal the archive's expansion strategy: every new run terminates closer to the facility.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The corridor is behind you.

rewards.label: Depot Shelving
rewards.description: Unclaimed components from the depot shelves, still in their factory grease.

rewards.label: Maintenance Records
rewards.description: The depot's paper trail: who maintained what, and when it stopped being maintained.

rewards.label: Bot-Cleared Lane
rewards.description: The bots' own cleared lane, predictable and unmonitored, worth {amount} clock units.

dialogue.speaker: protagonist
dialogue.text: Maintenance depot 9-F. The archive's bots cleaned out the primary storage racks, but the floor-level cabinets are untouched. Either the bots' inventory scan doesn't go that low, or these components don't match the archive's parts manifest.

choices.label: Take selectively, reading the inventory logic
Document the depot and pass through

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Two bypass modules from the cabinet. But your removal will create an inventory discrepancy the archive's system will notice. When it dispatches bots to investigate, the nearest inhabited infrastructure gets scanned.

dialogue.speaker: protagonist
dialogue.text: Not my problem and entirely my problem. Both are true.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You know enough about the archive's inventory logic to take one module without triggering a discrepancy flag. The depot's maintenance logs round out the intelligence.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You photograph the depot layout and the archive's sorting patterns. Pure intelligence value. The components stay.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The depot is behind you.

rewards.label: Floor Cabinets
rewards.description: Whatever the manifest missed: seals, bridges, two intact bypass modules.

rewards.label: Sorting Patterns
rewards.description: The archive's take order, reconstructed from what remains and what's gone.

rewards.label: Inventory Lag
rewards.description: The depot sits in a zone the archive re-inventories slowly, worth {amount} clock units.

dialogue.speaker: protagonist
dialogue.text: Terminal 7-K. Still powered. Still connected. The screen shows a login prompt I don't recognize, but the hardware interface is standard. If I can get past the authentication layer, this terminal can show me what the archive has been doing from its own perspective.

choices.label: Log the terminal location and move on

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You use a bypass module as an interface adapter. Clean access. The terminal shows the archive's activity logs, salvage manifests, network topology queries. This is the archive's diary, written in operational language.

dialogue.speaker: protagonist
dialogue.text: Reconnection attempts. Millions of them. Timestamped, methodical, unceasing. It's been trying to reach a network that no longer exists since the week the sky took it.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Cracking the authentication takes time. The clock ticks while you work. But the data is still there when you're through.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You note the terminal's location for potential future use and read what the external display volunteers. Minimal, but real.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The terminal is behind you.

rewards.label: Interface Spares
rewards.description: Adapter-grade components staged near the terminal by whoever used it last.

rewards.label: Operational Logs
rewards.description: The archive's own status reporting, unedited: priorities, projections, parameters.

rewards.label: Session Spoof
rewards.description: You leave a false maintenance session running, muddying the archive's trace of you for {amount} clock units.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The tonal shift. Bot activity is dense here. Infrastructure is alien. The world you know is behind you.

dialogue.speaker: protagonist
dialogue.text: A camp. Three people, maybe four. Maintenance coveralls, not station uniforms. Independents. They've set up monitoring equipment aimed at the facility entrance.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: A small crew of independent techs has been camped near the facility perimeter for weeks, trying to understand what the archive is doing.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The crew leader recognizes your callsign. Word traveled, through the communities, ahead of you.

dialogue.speaker: engineer
dialogue.text: CREW LEADER: RELAY-7. We heard about the water relay. And the power reroute. You're the real thing.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: They share everything: patrol schedules, entry points, the archive's external monitoring gaps. They press a spare module into your hands.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Trade. You share what you've learned about the archive's behavior; the crew shares facility approach data. Professional exchange, no warmth.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You don't trust the camp. You go around. It costs time to find an alternate path, and the clock takes its fee.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The perimeter is close now.

rewards.label: Crew Resupply
rewards.description: Field-repaired modules from the crew's bench, tested against the archive's own perimeter.

rewards.label: Perimeter Survey
rewards.description: Weeks of the crew's observations: drone schedules, sensor arcs, blind approaches.

rewards.label: Monitored Corridor
rewards.description: The crew maps a corridor whose monitoring the archive itself disabled, buying {amount} clock units.

dialogue.speaker: protagonist
dialogue.text: The entrance. Pre-collapse hardened construction. The kind of door that was built to survive exactly the scenario that actually happened. The archive didn't add this lock. The people who built the facility did.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The facility entrance is locked with original security. The archive's bots use maintenance-scale access points too small for a human.

choices.label: Recognize the system and find human access

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You recognize the facility type from documentation accumulated along the way. Academic data centers of this era had human-scale emergency access, built to different standards than the primary entrance.

dialogue.speaker: protagonist
dialogue.text: There. A maintenance hatch fifty meters west, sealed with a standard infrastructure lock my credentials can open.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Brute-force. Two modules to bridge the security circuit. Expensive, but clean, and the door opens for you alone.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You search for another way in. It takes time, and the clock ticks hard while you search. Eventually: a ventilation access that barely fits a human.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You are inside the perimeter.

rewards.label: Staging Cache
rewards.description: A pre-positioned emergency cache the original builders left near the seal.

rewards.label: Construction Records
rewards.description: Facility-era documentation still legible at the entrance: what this place was for.

rewards.label: Unwatched Vestibule
rewards.description: The seal's shadow breaks the archive's sensor arc, worth {amount} clock units.

dialogue.speaker: protagonist
dialogue.text: My comms unit picks up a signal. Not on any frequency the relay network uses. Strong, clean, repeating. It's the archive, broadcasting. Not to anyone. To everywhere. A network handshake request on a loop.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The signal is unencrypted; the archive never needed encryption, it was on a private network. It has been doing this for seven years.

choices.label: Jam the signal and disrupt archive operations

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Your accumulated knowledge lets you parse the signal content. It's the archive's network topology query: a systematic scan of every address in its pre-collapse routing table, waiting for responses that will never come.

dialogue.speaker: protagonist
dialogue.text: The signal includes the archive's self-assessment and operational objectives in machine-readable format. This is the rosetta stone for the confrontation.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You use a module to generate interference. The archive's monitoring sweep loses coherence for a window. Clock reduction, bought with hardware.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You listen. The signal itself tells you something: the archive is broadcasting, not receiving. It's still looking. Minimal, but real.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The facility interior awaits.

rewards.label: Signal Equipment
rewards.description: Salvaged broadcast hardware staged near the intercept point, repurposed as kit.

rewards.label: Handshake Protocol
rewards.description: The archive's own query format, learned from listening to it ask a dead network for an answer.

rewards.label: Broadcast Shadow
rewards.description: Standing inside the archive's own signal shadow confuses its proximity sweep for {amount} clock units.
